messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Valid days
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jairo,

I am able to process a 7 day Actigraph csv file here, so I am not sure whether there is a problem with GGIR.

1. As you may know csv-files can be cropped when you open and save them again: It truncates the length of a csv file. If that has happened and if Actilife is analysing the original data file then it is understandable that Actilife can still see all the days. To test this you could try to extract the csv file again and the re-process it with GGIR, but remember not to open and save the files.

2. Can it be that the participants did not reach the 16 hours valid day from the 5th day onward? What happens if you lower this criteria? If this is affecting the number of days included then it could be that other software use softer criteria.

3. Yes, setting to maxdur=0 makes that no days are excluded.

Best wishes, Vincent

Hi Vincent,

I have done some checks.

First, I thing that in g.part5, around the line 449 of the code in github, the code for the "firstlastexclude" argument is wrong. If you set it false, the code remove the last night, it should be the contrary, right?

Also, I have found another problem with our protocol. Our start of the measurement is at 6am, and we want to analyze this first day together with the following night (using a "WW" timewindow). But when the code search for the nights (nightsi), it look for 0am to define them. So, our first day/night is excluded. Would be possible to analyse this first day and night in GGIR assuming this protocol?

Thank you,
Jairo

messages.subject: ActiGraph users: csv file format
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am wondering if there is a specific format that the .csv files need to be in between downloading the raw data from ActiGraph (without time stamps) and importing them into R and analyzing the data with GGIR? I have tried running both g.inspectfile and the g.shell code and neither of them seem to recognize the file header.

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks,
Jess

messages.subject: Re: ActiGraph users: csv file format
messages.body_plain:
Hey Jess,

Like you, we are rather new to the package and still finding our way through the whole process. We started with a similar problem as you describe. If you have RAW.csv files than the file format is not the problem. In our case it turned out that the date format with hyphens as created by ActiLife was not recognised by GGIR. Vincent has fixed that for us. You can find the fix on github https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/releases/tag/v1.5-10

Maybe that helps.

Greetings from a fellow-newbee, Lily

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Valid days
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jairo,

No - changing it to TRUE will mess up the analyses for users who want to exclude the first and last night. Those two lines may actually need to be excluded. Note that I designed part5 for the Whitehall study in London. Any generic functionality for other studies is nice, but not something I can take responsibility for. It would take a couple of days to develop this further and carefully verify all use cases. I am very happy to talk to people about consultancy opportunities to do this and other work.

Cheers, Vincent

messages.subject: Very High ENMO Outputs When Recalibration Fails
messages.subject_clean: Very High ENMO Outputs When Recalibration Fails
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm processing some Geneactiv files with GGIR. I'm having a bit of trouble with the output which I'm hoping someone may have experienced before.

For files where the recalibration completes, the data looks good - the MVPA estimates are what I would expect. However, for files where the output in part 2 reads "recalibration not done because not enough points on all sides of the sphere", I get very high ENMO values (>400) and consequently very high MVPA output (>16 hours).

When I inspect the data plots I can see that the accelerometer values are too high (image attached). As you can see in the plot, there is a period of time before the device was actually worn, and i'm wondering if it's trying to calibrate using this data?

I've tried:
Running the script with do.imp = FALSE
With varying types of "strategy ="

I'm wondering if this is a problem with our protocol (i.e., with non-wear time at the beginning of the measurement period), a problem with the device (i.e., sensor problems), or something I can fix in GGIR?

Appreciate and suggestions.

Thanks,
Taren

Dear Taren,

we also had issues with some of our devices. If you look at the device numbers corresponding to the files with issues, do you find the same devices?
In our experience few devices started to have some weird results after some time (sometimes due to water inside the device), calibration method could not always correct for these issues and we had to exclude these devices and the recorded data from our analyses.

I hope this helps

Séverine

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] .csv file to analyse
messages.body_plain:
GGIR is not designed for analysing the submission checklists for the journal of neuroscience research ;)

Please ask Inacio, Alan or someone else from Pelotas to help you. They have experience with GGIR and may be able to help you quickly.
If you do run into a problem then please post it here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues. This email list is mainly intended for generic questions/discussions and not for help with specific problems.

If you do report a problem then please add as much detail as you can, as in: what accelerometer brand, study design, things you tried to fix it yourself, error messages you get. In that way you make it easier for others to help you.

Thanks
